About the Program
Smart Agriculture Energy Innovation Network

SAGEIN is a four-year, $3 million NSF Research Traineeship at Mississippi State University integrating engineering, agriculture, human sciences, and economics to address the intertwined challenges of energy, food, and rural economic development. The traineeship program begins Fall 2026.

Students from engineering, agriculture, economics, computer science, environmental science, data science, and related disciplines are all encouraged to apply. No prior energy background required.

Graduate Certificate
Certificate Program
🎓

Cross-Discipline Graduate Certificate

The SAGEIN Graduate Certificate is intentionally designed to span disciplines — open to graduate students across engineering, agriculture, economics, computer science, environmental science, data science, human sciences, and natural resources. Students bring expertise from their home department and develop convergent skills across the entire SAGEIN curriculum alongside peers from different fields.

One year · 12 credit hours · Complements your existing MS or PhD degree program

SemesterCourseTypeCredits

SummerPracticum Experience
Implementation or evaluation of a real-world distributed energy solution · professional project report and presentation		Required3

  • Real-world rural energy assessments with farms, Extension partners, and community stakeholders
  • Interdisciplinary training alongside peers from engineering, agriculture, economics, and beyond
  • AI and IoT skills for distributed energy optimization and precision agriculture
  • Entrepreneurship, intellectual property, and technology transfer training
  • Summer placement opportunities at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and industry partners
  • A competitive credential aligned with NSF national workforce priorities in Clean Energy, Biotechnology, and AI

NRT Traineeship Fellowship

$37,000
Annual Stipend + 1 Year Tuition Support

Competitive fellowship positions are available for eligible MS and PhD students. All applicants use a single form — simply check the fellowship box to be considered.

How to Apply
Apply to SAGEIN
1
Talk to your advisor
Get written approval confirming the certificate aligns with your degree plan and research progress.
2
Complete the application
Submit the form including a 500–750 word Statement of Purpose describing your interest and career goals.
3
Indicate fellowship interest
Check the fellowship box on the form to be considered for the $37,000 annual stipend and tuition support.
4
Submit by July 1
Applications for the Fall 2026 cohort are due July 1. Questions? Contact Ms. Santee Ezell.
Application Deadline: July 1 · Fall 2026 cohort · Contact Ms. Santee Ezell at se126@msstate.edu with any questions.
